threads.body: [Testing] In core-io 1.0.0, `shutdown()` returns a cold `Observable`: the I/O pool is shut down only when it is subscribed to. `deferAfterAll` accepts an `AutoCloseable`, so this method reference discards that observable and leaves the pool running after teardown. Neither cluster closes the explicitly supplied environment. Subscribe to and await the returned observable, while handling the synchronous boolean return used by the SDK 2.5 latest-dependency run.

@copilot Update this PR directly to fix the baseline fixture cleanup leak identified by Copilot review 5608824472, https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/20826#discussion_r4344178795. This is a scoped completion correction for the original isolated Couchbase SDK 2.0.0 baseline repair. Keep this PR draft. Do not create another PR.

In CouchbaseBaselineTest.java, cleanup.deferAfterAll(environment::shutdown) discards the return value. I verified the published core-io 1.0.0 source: DefaultCoreEnvironment.shutdown() returns a cold Observable<Boolean>; ioPool.shutdownGracefully() runs inside its subscription callback. I also verified java-client 2.0.0: both clusters are created with an explicitly supplied shared environment, and CouchbaseAsyncCluster.disconnect() deliberately skips environment.shutdown() for a shared environment. The new baseline fixture therefore leaks its I/O pool after class teardown. The latest-dependency suite also runs this fixture with SDK 2.5.x, where shutdown() returns a synchronous boolean instead. Published SDK 2.5.0 depends on core-io 1.5.0, whose shutdown() blocks on shutdownAsync().

Make the deferred class-scoped environment cleanup actually subscribe to and await completion on the oldest runtime, with a bounded wait and explicit failure propagation, while remaining compatible with the synchronous boolean API in the existing pinned-latest suite. Preserve the current deferred resource ownership and teardown ordering so clusters disconnect before the supplied environment shuts down and partially initialized setup remains protected. Use the simplest type-safe solution appropriate to this fixture. Do not silently discard a shutdown failure or add a broad compatibility fallback. Keep production instrumentation, dependency floors, suite isolation, retained 2.5/2.6 coverage and telemetry unchanged.

Run the narrowest applicable formatter immediately before behavioral validation. Exercise the default and experimental baseline suites with SDK 2.0.0/core-io 1.0.0 and in the existing latest-dependency mode, covering cleanup completion in both API shapes. Preserve or add focused coverage only as needed to establish that shutdown really completes; successful operations alone do not prove resource cleanup. Report exact commands and outcomes, and any concrete environmental blocker. Do not use clean or --rerun-tasks, and do not change unrelated modules or PR metadata.

@copilot Update this existing PR directly with the following two simplifications, preserving its current draft/ready state. Keep the work scoped to these simplifications rather than creating a separate PR.

In CouchbaseBucketInstrumentation.java, merge CouchbaseClientAdvice and CouchbaseClientQueryAdvice into one bucket advice. They now duplicate call-depth tracking, request-context scope handling, and returned-observable wrapping. Bind the optional first argument and interpret it as a query only when methodName.equals("query"); other methods must retain operation-based request construction regardless of their first argument. Preserve the existing null-query fallback. Choose queryInstrumenter() versus instrumenter() using request.isSqlQuery(). Preserve request context during observable assembly, scope restoration on normal and exceptional exits, balanced call-depth tracking, null-result handling, and independent per-subscription copies. Keep normal and query telemetry unchanged, including query sanitization.

In CouchbaseBaselineTest.java, reuse the opened bucket's async interface: after bucket = cluster.openBucket(BUCKET_NAME, PASSWORD), assign asyncBucket = bucket.async(). Bucket.async() is available in SDK 2.0.0. Remove the separate CouchbaseAsyncCluster construction, its extra bucket-open operation and disconnect callback, and the now-unused import. Adjust the setup trace drain from two traces to one. Retain both synchronous and asynchronous operation tests, including the nested-callback parent relationship asserted by the async test.

Keep the isolated SDK 2.0.0/core-io 1.0.0 baseline, version25Test and version26Test suites, query and Spring Data coverage, and the existing assemblyRequest late-network-capture fallback. Do not replace that fallback with a one-time node copy or shared mutable subscription state. Leave the bounded environment-shutdown adapter and deferred cleanup ordering intact; it handles both the old Observable and newer boolean shutdown APIs. Avoid introducing an advice-state hierarchy or unrelated refactoring.

Run the narrowest applicable formatter immediately before relevant behavioral validation. Exercise the default and experimental baseline tests and retained SDK 2.5/2.6 tests covering ordinary operations, queries, sanitization, Spring Data, and repeated subscription where feasible. Preserve supported dependency floors and report concrete environmental blockers rather than changing unrelated build behavior. Do not use clean or --rerun-tasks.

threads.body: [Javaagent] Replace the new `Context.current()` calls in both `trackCallDepth()` and `subscribeResult()` in this class and `CouchbaseClusterInstrumentation` with `Java8BytecodeBridge.currentContext()`. Classic instrumentation can inline annotated advice even when its source specifies `inline = false`; copying a static interface call into pre-Java-8 bytecode can cause class verification errors. This is the bridge convention documented in `.github/instructions/javaagent.instructions.md:92` and the compatibility constraint described by `Java8BytecodeBridge`. Import the bridge in both files and remove the unused `Context` imports after replacing all four calls.

replies.body: No change needed. At 377e853f, all advice registered by `CouchbaseInstrumentationModule` has `inline = false`, and the module does not override the helper strategy. `AdviceInspector` selects isolated advice for `ALL_NON_INLINE`; `InstrumentationModuleInstaller.useIndy()` follows that selection, and `IndyTypeTransformerImpl` installs invokedynamic dispatch rather than copying the advice bodies into target classes. The four `Context.current()` calls therefore remain in separately compiled advice classes. Restoring the bridge here would undo the requested correction without addressing a supported inlining path.
